limits: PASS is the scoped owned native run, never global H19 acceptance.
Mock Keychain is an explicit Chromium test backend, not a production fix.
Frame acquisition is not audiovisual output FPS. No CEF timestamp is PTS.
Python and native clocks are analyzed separately.
Only observed PID/birth identities are proven cleaned; this is not hostile process confinement.

process_observer.scope: same-user process metadata; observed tree only, not hostile confinement

last_10_seconds.memory_note: Sequential sums; RSS can double-count shared pages. Footprint is not unique physical RAM.

startup_warmup.memory_note: Sequential sums; RSS can double-count shared pages. Footprint is not unique physical RAM.

steady.memory_note: Sequential sums; RSS can double-count shared pages. Footprint is not unique physical RAM.

static_inventory.scope: static artifact identity and local development signature

resource_measurements.cpu_unit: nanoseconds; percent 100 equals one fully occupied core
limits: Only consecutive observations of matching PID/birth/start identity contribute CPU deltas.
CPU before first/after last observation and processes shorter than the sampling interval may be missed.
Memory is a sequential sum of per-process physical footprints, not a coalition or unique physical-page total.
Reported CPU excludes the supervisor and process-list collection overhead.
Roles parse a finite allowlist of owned helper process arguments, birth checked before/after; no raw command line retained.
Virtual bytes are address-space reservation; private/shared residency and unique physical pages remain unavailable.
Historical cpu_percent_ps remains ps output; legacy footprint_bytes remains unspecified/null.

rss_budget.scope: sampled emergency stop, not a hard allocation cap; intersample peaks may be missed

supervision.scope: observed owned tree; not proof against unobserved process escape or an OS sandbox
